name: Oral antibiotics (doxycycline/minocycline)
lead: Doxycycline and minocycline are tetracycline-class antibiotics that dermatologists prescribe for inflammatory acne and rosacea. They are used to calm red, swollen pimples and the redness and bumps of rosacea, which is how they improve the look of the skin; both are prescription-only in the US and other countries [1][2][9][11].

Wikipedia reports that doxycycline is used at higher doses for severe acne and rosacea and at lower subantimicrobial doses long term, with benefit thought to come partly from anti-inflammatory effects [1]. Minocycline is approved for inflammatory lesions of moderate-to-severe acne in people aged nine and older, with oral courses typically three to four months and limited data beyond that [2]. Because of antibiotic resistance, oral antibiotics are generally combined with topical acne treatments such as benzoyl peroxide or a retinoid [2][9].

A JAMA review describes topical retinoids, benzoyl peroxide and azelaic acid as first-line acne treatments, with oral antibiotics among the systemic options added for more inflammatory disease [12]. In looksmaxxing forums, oral antibiotics come up as an option for stubborn acne, alongside retinoids, and some posters voice concerns about gut flora [8].

chain: The drug reduces inflammation and bacterial load in the skin
Inflamed papules and pustules calm down over weeks
angle.text: Doxycycline and minocycline reduce the inflamed lesions of acne and rosacea, so the visible result is fewer red, swollen spots over roughly two to three months. They are prescribed by dermatologists and are usually paired with topicals.

infobox: About 3 to 4 months for minocycline [2]; Acne article: no more than 3 months recommended [9]

paras: Both drugs treat a range of infections. Doxycycline is used for respiratory and urinary infections, chlamydia, Lyme disease and many others, and is common for acne and rosacea [1]. Minocycline is used for inflammatory acne and is described as generally less preferred than doxycycline for other infections [2].

For acne, oral antibiotics kill Cutibacterium acnes and reduce inflammation; Wikipedia says they work better than topical antibiotics and clear inflammatory lesions faster, and that acne generally improves 8 to 12 weeks after starting therapy [9]. The JAMA review notes that acne affects roughly 9 percent of the population worldwide and about 85 percent of people aged 12 to 24, can cause permanent scarring, and is associated with lowered quality of life and self-image, which is why treating inflammation early is a recurring theme in dermatology [12].

For rosacea, Wikipedia says oral doxycycline is the oral option most clinicians prefer, usually as a low-dose modified-release capsule taken for anti-inflammatory effect, and that these drugs reduce papules and pustules mainly through anti-inflammatory action rather than antibacterial action [11]. Rosacea causes facial redness, papules and pustules, and the article notes that visible symptoms can affect self-esteem and social life; treatments often bring temporary remission, and redness usually returns after treatment stops [11].

Wikipedia describes low-dose doxycycline (40 mg daily) as appearing as effective as 100 mg with fewer gastrointestinal effects, though not FDA-approved for acne [9]. Dermatologists generally prefer antibiotics as part of combination therapy rather than alone, and Wikipedia reports that guidelines advise limiting oral antibiotic courses to about three months, adding benzoyl peroxide or a retinoid if they must continue [9].

Doxycycline is also used for Lyme disease, malaria prevention and, since 2024 US guidance, as post-exposure prophylaxis for bacterial sexually transmitted infections in certain groups [1][17]. Minocycline is used for skin infections including some MRSA, and a topical foam is used for acne and rosacea [2].

A systematic review and network meta-analysis of 179 randomized trials with about 35,000 observations compared topical, oral, physical and combined treatments for mild-to-moderate and moderate-to-severe acne, measuring percentage change in total lesion count, so oral antibiotics sit within a wider ranking of options [13]. Wikipedia reports that minocycline and doxycycline have similar effectiveness for acne, though doxycycline may carry a slightly lower risk of side effects [2].

A 2014 review cited by Wikipedia found oral antibiotics somewhat more effective than birth control pills for inflammatory lesions at three months, but roughly equal at six months, and a 2018 review found no difference in inflammatory lesions between antibiotics and isotretinoin [9]. Isotretinoin remains the usual choice for severe nodular acne, with about half or more people reaching complete remission after one course, according to the same article [9].

Doxycycline: diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, increased sunburn risk, and pill esophagitis if taken without enough fluid. It is FDA pregnancy category D and is not recommended in pregnancy [1]. One large retrospective study cited by Wikipedia found a 2.25-fold higher Crohn's disease risk in patients prescribed it for acne [1]. Doxycycline is contraindicated with isotretinoin because both can rarely cause intracranial hypertension [1].

Minocycline: long-term use can cause blue-gray pigmentation of skin, nails and scars, which can take very long to fade, with muddy brown pigmentation in sun-exposed skin usually permanent [2]. It can cause drug-induced lupus and autoimmune hepatitis, more often in women, and DRESS syndrome in the first weeks [2]. Vestibular effects such as dizziness and tinnitus are described as particular to minocycline among the tetracyclines, and rarely intracranial hypertension [2]. The US label warns that tetracycline-class drugs can cause fetal harm and permanent tooth discoloration if used during tooth development [3].
Tetracyclines as a class can cause phototoxicity, and expired products can form a degradation product linked to kidney toxicity, so expired prescriptions are discarded [10][2].

Both are mainly bacteriostatic, binding the 30S ribosomal subunit and inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis [1][2][3][10]. Doxycycline also reduces neutrophil chemotaxis and inhibits matrix metalloproteinases and kallikrein 5, which lowers the cathelicidin peptide LL-37 linked to rosacea inflammation [1]. Experts still debate whether the benefit in acne and rosacea comes mainly from antibacterial or anti-inflammatory effects, and subantimicrobial dosing is thought probably not to drive resistance [1].

Minocycline is the most lipophilic tetracycline and crosses the blood-brain barrier better than doxycycline [2]. A review of non-antibiotic effects describes anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, anti-apoptotic and immunomodulatory activity for both drugs [16].

Wikipedia reports that heavy broad-spectrum use has raised rates of resistant C. acnes, especially to tetracyclines and topical macrolides, and that several guidelines urge providers to prescribe oral antibiotics less, though they remain the most commonly prescribed systemic acne therapy [9]. The Global Alliance to Improve Outcomes in Acne advises against combining topical and oral antibiotics [9]. Tetracycline resistance occurs through efflux pumps, ribosomal protection and other mechanisms, and resistance genes spread by horizontal gene transfer [10]. A narrower-spectrum tetracycline, sarecycline, is FDA-approved for moderate to severe inflammatory acne from age nine [9].

A randomized trial in adult women, the FASCE study, compared spironolactone with doxycycline in moderate acne in a multicentre, double-blind design [14]. Registered trials include a 528-person phase 3 trial of 40 mg doxycycline versus placebo in rosacea [4], a comparison of spironolactone versus doxycycline for acne (n=350) [5], and a trial of metformin versus doxycycline in adult acne [6]. A study of subantimicrobial doxycycline in acne has also been registered [7]. Reviews of rosacea management discuss tetracyclines among oral options [15]. Studies of minocycline in stroke and neurodegeneration are not related to appearance use [16].

Tetracyclines were first reported in 1948, when chlortetracycline was derived from a soil bacterium at Lederle Laboratories, with oxytetracycline following in 1949 [10]. Doxycycline was developed at Pfizer, patented in 1957 and FDA-approved in 1967 [1]. A patent dispute over it with International Rectifier ran until 1983 and was described by Wikipedia as the largest litigated patent case in US history [1]. Minocycline was patented in 1961 and sold from 1971; a topical acne foam was approved in 2019 [2]. In 2013 the FDA reported doxycycline shortages, and prices of a 500-tablet bottle rose steeply before falling [1].

On looksmax.org, one user described taking a high amount of minocycline with persistent acne and asked about adding a second antibiotic. Replies said diet matters, that antibiotics disrupt gut flora, and suggested retinoid-based topicals instead [8]. On the bodybuilding forum T Nation, users discussing testosterone therapy have mentioned minocycline or doxycycline for body acne, though these are forum anecdotes.

timeline.event: Chlortetracycline, the first tetracycline, is reported [10].
Pfizer patent dispute over doxycycline resolved [1].
Topical minocycline foam approved for acne [2].
JAMA publishes a review on the management of acne vulgaris [12].
Network meta-analysis of 179 acne trials published [13].
FASCE trial of spironolactone versus doxycycline in adult women published [14].

lore.intro: Forum users discuss oral antibiotics for stubborn acne and debate gut effects, and often compare them with retinoids [8].

claims.claim: Antibiotics destroy gut flora and should be avoided unless truly needed
claims.believers: A looksmax.org reply said antibiotics damage gut flora and recommended retinoid products instead [8].
claims.experts: Wikipedia notes that resistance is a growing concern leading clinicians to combine oral antibiotics with topicals and limit courses to around three months [2][9]. Studies of gut effects of acne antibiotics were not found.

claims.claim: Diet is the key lever for acne, more than medication
claims.believers: A looksmax.org reply said fixing diet is key for reducing acne [8].
claims.experts: The JAMA review lists topical retinoids and benzoyl peroxide as first-line treatments, with oral antibiotics and other systemic agents for more inflammatory disease [12].

claims.claim: A second antibiotic can be added when one does not clear acne
claims.believers: A poster asked whether adding a second antibiotic on top of minocycline would help [8].
claims.experts: No published trial found tests stacking a second oral antibiotic on minocycline for acne. Wikipedia reports guidelines advise limiting oral antibiotic courses to about three months and using benzoyl peroxide or a retinoid alongside them [9].

claims.claim: Retinoids are the better route to clear skin than antibiotics
claims.believers: Replies pointed to vitamin A products and derivatives rather than antibiotics [8].
claims.experts: Wikipedia reports a 2018 review found no difference in inflammatory lesions between antibiotics and isotretinoin, and that isotretinoin causes about twice as many adverse events, mostly dryness [9].

claims.claim: Low-dose doxycycline works for rosacea without acting as an antibiotic
claims.believers: Dermatology sources describe low-dose modified-release doxycycline as working through anti-inflammatory effects [11].
claims.experts: Wikipedia says experts still debate whether the benefit comes mainly from antibacterial or anti-inflammatory effects [1].

card.summary: Prescription tetracyclines for inflammatory acne; established in dermatology, with documented side effects and resistance concerns.
card.note: Pregnancy and tooth-development warnings; minocycline pigmentation and lupus-like reactions.

quick.overview:
Doxycycline and minocycline are oral antibiotics that dermatologists prescribe for inflammatory acne and rosacea. They are usually paired with topical treatments.

Forum users discuss them for stubborn acne, with some voicing gut-health concerns.
quick.mechanism: They inhibit bacterial protein synthesis and also have anti-inflammatory effects.
quick.risks: Doxycycline: GI upset, sun sensitivity, esophagitis. Minocycline: pigmentation, drug-induced lupus, dizziness, rare intracranial hypertension. Both are warned against in pregnancy and childhood tooth development. Prescription-only.
